6. Charge, energy and exact renewal operation

At6mC/cm2 and25cm2 the passed charge is.15C. An introduced10V pulse costs1.5J in the interfacial electrical boundary; equal forward/reverse pulses would cost3J there. This does not pay for control, preparation, contact establishment, mechanical peeling, heating, cleaning or restoring humidity.

If all that charge were irreversibly assigned to Cu2+ dissolution, Faraday's law gives49.3956ugCu percycle,2.20516nm over the stated area, and1.10258um after500cycles using introducedCu density8960kg/m3. This is an inventory scenario, not measured corrosion or an inevitable loss. Equal reverse charge does not prove copper returns to the original location, oxidation state, roughness or interface; a side reaction or spatially uneven plating can leave a different bond despite netzero charge.

For500 identical fractional-loss cycles and95% retained inventory, the loss fraction percycle must be<=1-.95^(1/500)=.0001025813, or.0102581%. Other replenishment/recovery laws remain possible if their material, waste and energy costs are paid. A meaningful closed cycle must track actual film, counterions, water, electrode morphology and bondable contact area, not only Coulombs.

A plausible but unconstructed mechanism is an array of supported reversible bond cells: conform during engagement, distribute load without concentrating peel at a few cells, mechanically hold the established state, then unload externally, create a controlled low-energy crack path and restore the same material. Each support, seal, addressing electrode, contact sensor, current route, release path and maintenance step must be manufactured and paid. Permanent geometric fasteners or dry adhesives may still dominate. The actual useful opening is repeated load-bearing attachment with bounded restoration; it is not electrochemical disbonding by name or an ideal universal assembly theorem.

These scripts and contracts introduce no qualified joint, buyer advantage, current component price, physical execution or general impossibility claim.
